observation_summary: The compiler was incorrectly coalescing variables in sort functions, causing IE runtime errors, and failing to correctly parse JSDoc license blocks containing annotations.
reasoning_summary: The fix in CoalesceVariableNames adds a conditional check to identify sort functions and mark parameters as escaped, preventing incorrect optimization. The fix in JsDocInfoParser adds a conditional guard to prevent incorrect token processing during license block parsing. Both fixes are fundamentally about adding missing validation logic (guards) to handle specific edge cases correctly.
evidence_used: The fix in CoalesceVariableNames adds an 'if' condition to check the child count of the scope node before marking parameters as escaped.
The fix in JsDocInfoParser adds an 'if' condition to check the current option and token type before proceeding with extraction.
The bug report explicitly mentions an IE bug related to variable coalescing in sort functions, which the fix addresses by adding a guard.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes the behavior of the optimization, the root cause is the absence of a guard to prevent the optimization from running in unsafe contexts (IE sort bug).
The fix does not require a new design-level capability, but rather a refinement of existing logic via conditional checks.
